result:
At the edge of the harbor, a gull stood perfectly still, as if it had been asked to guard the morning.

Boats knocked gently against their moorings. The water kept changing its mind about the color of the sky. Somewhere behind me, a café door opened and released the smell of coffee into the cold.

I watched the gull until it lifted its wings and disappeared over the roofs. Nothing dramatic happened. The harbor stayed a harbor. The morning went on being morning.

Still, for a little while, the world had seemed to pause—not because anything had stopped, but because I had finally stood still enough to notice it moving.
